clips.send: Timpani. Percussion, tuned drums. A pedal stretches the drumhead tighter to raise the pitch. Usually 2 to 5 drums per player. Tighter head, faster vibration, higher pitch (just like the string lab!).

clips.send: Tanggu and gong 堂鼓·锣. Percussion, the energy of festivals and opera. 堂鼓 tánggǔ: a barrel drum played with two sticks. The gong 锣 and cymbals 镲 add crashes; in Peking opera the percussion section leads the whole show. Drum + gong patterns are called 锣鼓经 luógǔjīng.

clips.send: Violin. Strings, the orchestra’s melody voice. Four strings tuned G–D–A–E, each a 5th apart. The bow is horsehair rubbed with rosin so it grips the string. A full orchestra has about 30 violins, in “first” and “second” groups.

clips.send: Dizi 笛子 dízi. Winds, bamboo flute. A bamboo transverse flute with six finger holes. Its secret: an extra hole covered with a thin membrane 笛膜 that buzzes — the bright, reedy sound. Bone flutes found at Jiahu (贾湖), Henan, are about 8,000–9,000 years old.

clips.send: Sheng 笙 shēng. Winds, mouth organ with free reeds. A bundle of bamboo pipes, each with a small metal reed. It can play chords — rare for a wind instrument. It is about 3,000 years old (it appears in the 《诗经》 Book of Songs). The free-reed idea later inspired the harmonica and the accordion.

clips.send: Guzheng 古筝 gǔzhēng. Plucked strings, zither with moving bridges. Usually 21 strings, each with its own movable bridge. Tuned to the pentatonic scale (宫商角徵羽), so sweeping glissandos always sound good. Pressing the string left of the bridge bends the pitch up — that adds the “missing” notes. Its ancestor, the 秦筝, is more than 2,000 years old.

clips.send: Erhu 二胡 èrhú. Bowed strings, the “Chinese violin”. Just two strings, tuned D4 and A4 — a 5th apart. The bow hair runs BETWEEN the two strings. No fingerboard: fingers press the strings in mid-air, so slides and wide vibrato are easy. Famous piece: 《二泉映月》 “The Moon Reflected in Erquan Spring” by the blind street musician 阿炳 Abing (1893–1950).

clips.send: Flute. Woodwind, edge-blown. You blow across a hole, like blowing over a bottle — no reed. Range about C4 to C7. It is a woodwind even though it is made of metal.

clips.send: Pipa 琵琶 pípa. Plucked strings, pear-shaped lute. Four strings and many frets on a pear-shaped body. Players pluck with fingernails; the fast “wheel” tremolo 轮指 sounds like a shimmer. It has been in China for about 2,000 years. Famous piece: 《十面埋伏》 “Ambush from Ten Sides” — a whole battle told on one instrument.

clips.send: Clarinet. Woodwind, single reed. A single cane reed vibrates against the mouthpiece. Its straight, tube-shaped bore makes mostly odd harmonics (1, 3, 5…) — that is its hollow sound. Our synthesizer copies this with a square wave, which has only odd harmonics.

clips.send: 琵琶。弹拨乐器 · 梨形的弹拨乐器。梨形琴身，四根弦，很多品。 用指甲弹；快速的“轮指”像流水般闪烁。 在中国已有约 2000 年历史。 名曲：《十面埋伏》——用一件乐器讲完一整场战斗。

clips.send: 古筝。弹拨乐器 · 带活动琴码的筝。通常有 21 根弦，每根弦有一个可以移动的琴码。 按五声音阶（宫商角徵羽）定弦，所以“刮奏”怎么刮都好听。 按压琴码左边的弦可以把音推高，补出五声以外的音。 它的祖先“秦筝”已有 2000 多年历史。

clips.send: 笙。吹管乐器 · 带自由簧的“口琴”。一束竹管，每根管里有一片小铜簧。 能吹和弦——在管乐器里很少见。 约有 3000 年历史（《诗经》里就有“吹笙鼓簧”）。 自由簧的原理后来启发了口琴和手风琴。

clips.send: 二胡。拉弦乐器 · “中国小提琴”。只有两根弦，定弦 D4 和 A4，相差五度。 弓毛夹在两根弦之间。 没有指板：手指悬空按弦，所以滑音和宽揉弦很容易。 名曲：盲人民间艺人阿炳（华彦钧，1893—1950）的《二泉映月》。

clips.send: 笛子。吹管乐器 · 竹笛。横吹的竹笛，有六个按音孔。 它的秘密：一个贴着薄薄“笛膜”的膜孔，吹奏时笛膜振动，声音明亮带“沙”。 河南贾湖出土的骨笛距今约 8000—9000 年。

clips.send: 小提琴。弦乐 · 乐队的主旋律声部。四根弦定弦为 G—D—A—E，相邻两弦相差五度。 琴弓用马尾毛制成，涂上松香才能“抓住”琴弦。 一支完整的乐队约有 30 把小提琴，分“第一”和“第二”两组。

clips.send: 定音鼓。打击乐 · 能定音高的鼓。踏板把鼓皮绷紧，音就升高。 一个演奏者通常有 2 到 5 面鼓。 鼓皮越紧，振动越快，音越高（和琴弦实验一样！）。

clips.send: 单簧管。木管 · 单簧片。一片芦苇簧片贴着吹嘴振动。 直筒形的管身主要产生奇数次泛音（1、3、5……），所以声音有点“空”。 本页合成器用方波来模仿它——方波只有奇数次泛音。
